recipes.title: Steamed Sona Masoori Rice
recipes.description: Soft, separate grains of everyday sona masoori rice, cooked in a pressure cooker or an open pot. The base for sambar, rasam, kootu and curries. One serving = about 1 cup cooked rice (70 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Put the rice in the pressure-cooker pan, cover with water and rub the grains gently between your fingers. Drain and repeat two or three times until the water runs almost clear. This removes surface starch so the grains stay separate.
steps.visual: Raw white sona masoori rice under cloudy rinse water in a steel pressure-cooker pan, a hand swirling the grains

steps.title: Soak briefly
steps.text: Drain the rice, add the 3 cups of measured water and leave it to soak for 20 minutes. Soaked rice cooks more evenly and needs less time on the stove.
steps.visual: Rinsed rice resting under clear water in the same steel pressure-cooker pan on the counter, the grains turned opaque white

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Close the cooker and cook on medium heat for 2 whistles, about 8 to 10 minutes, then turn off the heat. For an open pot, bring to a boil, cover tightly and cook on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until all the water is absorbed.
steps.visual: The pressure cooker with its lid locked on a medium gas flame, the whistle lifting with a puff of steam

steps.title: Let the pressure drop
steps.text: Leave the cooker undisturbed for 10 minutes until the pressure settles on its own. The rice finishes cooking in the trapped steam.
steps.visual: The closed pressure cooker sitting off the flame on the stove top, no steam escaping

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Open the lid and fluff the rice gently with a flat spoon, lifting from the bottom so the grains don't break. Serve hot with sambar, dal or a curry and a vegetable side.
steps.visual: Fluffy white rice with distinct grains in a steel serving bowl, a ladle of sambar and a small bowl of beans poriyal beside it

substitutions.note: Brown rice needs a 30-minute soak and 4 to 5 whistles; it has more fibre per serving.
Foxtail millet cooks in 2 whistles with 2½ cups water per cup and has more fibre and protein than white rice.

recipes.storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate within an hour; use within 1 day.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with a tablespoon of water and microwave covered for 1 to 2 minutes, or steam until piping hot.

recipes.title: Kerala Matta Rice (Boiled and Drained)
recipes.description: Plump, nutty red matta rice cooked the Kerala way in plenty of water and then drained, which keeps the grains separate. Made for fish curry, sambar and thoran. One serving = about 1 cup cooked rice (70 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Wash the matta rice in a large bowl of water, rubbing the grains, and drain. Repeat twice; the water will stay slightly pink from the bran.
steps.visual: Reddish-brown matta rice grains in a steel bowl of pinkish rinse water, fingers rubbing the grains

steps.title: Soak for an hour
steps.text: Cover the rice with fresh water and soak for 1 hour. This cuts the boiling time by about 10 minutes and helps the thick grains cook through evenly.
steps.visual: Matta rice soaking under clear water in the same steel bowl, the grains slightly swollen

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Bring 8 cups of water to a rolling boil in a large, deep saucepan and add the salt.
steps.visual: A large, deep steel saucepan of water at a rolling boil on a high gas flame

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and add it to the boiling water. Cook uncovered on medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until a grain pressed between your fingers is soft with no hard centre. In a pressure cooker, use 5 cups water, cook for 5 to 6 whistles and then drain.
steps.visual: Plump red matta rice grains tumbling in bubbling, cloudy starch water in the deep steel saucepan, a wooden spoon resting across the rim

steps.title: Drain the starch water
steps.text: Hold the lid slightly ajar and pour off the starchy water (kanji vellam), or tip the rice into a colander. Keep the water to drink warm with a pinch of salt if you like.
steps.visual: Cloudy white starch water pouring from the tilted saucepan through a gap under the lid, the cooked red rice held back inside

steps.title: Rest covered
steps.text: Cover and leave for 5 minutes so the last of the moisture steams off and the grains firm up.
steps.visual: Drained matta rice steaming gently in the covered steel saucepan on the switched-off stove

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fluff with a spoon and serve hot with fish curry, sambar or moru curry and a vegetable thoran.
steps.visual: Fat, separate red matta rice grains on a banana leaf with a ladle of red fish curry and green cabbage thoran beside them

substitutions.note: Sona masoori cooks in a quarter of the time but has less fibre; use the absorption method instead of draining.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate in a closed box for up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Steam or microwave covered with a splash of water until hot right through.

recipes.title: Fluffy Pressure-Cooked Brown Rice
recipes.description: Chewy, nutty whole-grain rice with separate grains, using a soak and gentle pressure cooking so it is never hard in the centre. Pairs with dal, rajma or any curry. One serving = about 1 cup cooked (65 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Rinse the brown rice in the pressure-cooker pan two or three times and drain well.
steps.visual: Light tan brown-rice grains under rinse water in a steel pressure-cooker pan

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Add the 2½ cups of measured water and soak for 30 minutes. Brown rice keeps its bran layer, and soaking lets water reach the centre of the grain.
steps.visual: Brown rice soaking under clear water in the same steel pressure-cooker pan

steps.title: Season the water
steps.text: Stir in the salt and the oil, if using. The oil helps keep the grains separate and reduces foaming in the cooker.
steps.visual: A few drops of oil glistening on the water above the soaked brown rice in the cooker pan, a spoon stirring in the salt

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Close the lid and cook on medium heat for 4 whistles, then lower the heat and cook 5 minutes more. In an open pot, use 3 cups water, cover and cook on low heat for 40 to 45 minutes.
steps.visual: The closed pressure cooker on a medium gas flame with steam puffing from the whistle

steps.title: Natural release
steps.text: Turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own, about 15 minutes. Opening it early leaves the grains wet.
steps.visual: The pressure cooker resting off the heat on the stove top, the whistle settled

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Fluff with a fork and serve with dal, rajma, or a chicken or paneer curry.
steps.visual: Separate, plump brown-rice grains piled in a ceramic bowl with steam rising, a bowl of rajma beside it

substitutions.note: Kerala matta rice is another whole-bran rice; boil it in plenty of water and drain instead.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; brown rice holds its texture well in lunch boxes.
recipes.reheating: Microwave covered with 1 tbsp water for 2 minutes, or stir in a hot pan until steaming.

recipes.title: Foxtail Millet (Thinai) Rice
recipes.description: Light, fluffy foxtail millet cooked by the absorption method in a covered pot, an everyday swap for rice with sambar, kuzhambu and poriyal. One serving = about ¾ cup cooked (65 g raw).

steps.title: Wash well
steps.text: Rinse the millet in a bowl 3 to 4 times, swishing well, as the tiny grains can hold dust and husk. Drain through a fine sieve.
steps.visual: Tiny pale-yellow foxtail millet grains in a steel bowl of cloudy water, a few husks floating on top

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover the millet with fresh water and soak for 30 minutes, then drain.
steps.visual: Foxtail millet soaking under clear water in the same steel bowl

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Bring the 2¼ cups of measured water to a boil in a heavy saucepan with the salt and the ghee, if using.
steps.visual: Water at a rolling boil in a heavy-bottomed steel saucepan, a little ghee shimmering on the surface

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Add the drained millet, stir once, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 to 15 minutes until all the water is absorbed and small steam holes appear on the surface. In a pressure cooker, use 2 cups water and cook for 2 whistles.
steps.visual: Cooked foxtail millet in the uncovered steel saucepan, its surface dotted with small steam holes and no water left

steps.title: Rest and fluff
steps.text: Turn off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork.
steps.visual: Fluffed, separate millet grains in the saucepan with a fork lifting them

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with sambar, rasam or kuzhambu and a vegetable poriyal, just as you would serve rice.
steps.visual: A mound of fluffy pale-gold foxtail millet on a steel plate with sambar poured over one side and carrot poriyal beside it

substitutions.note: Little millet (samai) cooks the same way with 2 cups water per cup and turns slightly softer.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and steam or microwave covered; millet dries out faster than rice.

recipes.title: Little Millet (Samai) Rice in a Pressure Cooker
recipes.description: Soft samai rice cooked with a short soak and two whistles. Its mild taste suits rasam, sambar, dry curries and curd. One serving = about ¾ cup cooked (65 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse the millet
steps.text: Wash the samai in the pressure-cooker pan 3 to 4 times, swirling well, and drain carefully through a fine sieve so no grains escape.
steps.visual: Tiny cream-coloured little-millet grains in cloudy rinse water in a steel pressure-cooker pan

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Add the 2 cups of measured water and soak for 20 minutes.
steps.visual: Little millet soaking under clear water in the same steel cooker pan

steps.title: Add salt and oil
steps.text: Stir in the salt and a few drops of sesame oil, if using, to keep the grains from clumping.
steps.visual: A spoon stirring salt into the water over the soaked millet, a few golden drops of sesame oil floating on top

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Close the cooker and cook on medium heat for 2 whistles, about 8 minutes, then turn off the heat.
steps.visual: The pressure cooker on a medium flame letting out its second whistle in a burst of steam

steps.title: Release and fluff
steps.text: Let the pressure drop naturally, about 10 minutes, then open and fluff the millet gently with a fork.
steps.visual: The opened cooker showing soft, fluffed little-millet rice with steam rising from it

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with sambar, rasam or a dry curry, or cool it and mix with curd.
steps.visual: Soft samai rice in a brass bowl beside a small bowl of tomato rasam and a spoonful of beans poriyal

substitutions.note: Foxtail millet works the same way; add ¼ cup more water as it is slightly firmer.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Steam or microwave covered with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.title: Whole-Wheat Phulka
recipes.description: Thin, soft, puffed whole-wheat flatbreads cooked on a tawa and finished over the flame, with no oil in the dough. Makes 10 phulkas; one serving = 2 phulkas.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the atta and salt in a wide bowl. Add the water a little at a time, mixing with your fingers, until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
steps.visual: Soft, smooth light-brown wheat dough being kneaded with the knuckles in a wide steel mixing bowl, a little flour on the rim

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Cover the bowl and rest the dough for 20 minutes. Resting relaxes the gluten so the phulkas roll thin without shrinking back.
steps.visual: The ball of dough covered with a damp cloth in the same steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Divide into balls
steps.text: Knead the dough briefly again and divide it into 10 equal balls of about 50 g each. Keep them covered while you work.
steps.visual: Ten smooth, equal dough balls lined up on a steel plate beside the empty mixing bowl

steps.title: Roll thin
steps.text: Dip a ball in the dusting flour and roll it into an even 6-inch circle, turning it as you roll. Even thickness is what makes a phulka puff.
steps.visual: A thin, round dough circle on a wooden rolling board with a rolling pin, a small plate of dusting flour beside it

steps.title: Cook on the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium-high heat. Place the rolled phulka on it and cook about 20 seconds until small bubbles appear, then flip and cook the other side for 30 to 40 seconds until light brown spots form.
steps.visual: A thin phulka on a hot black iron tawa, its surface dotted with small bubbles and pale brown spots

steps.title: Puff over the flame
steps.text: Lift the phulka with tongs and hold it, first-cooked side down, directly over the open flame for a few seconds until it balloons. Flip for 2 seconds. On an induction hob, press the edges gently with a folded cloth on the tawa instead.
steps.visual: A fully puffed, balloon-like phulka held with steel tongs over a blue gas flame, light brown spots on its surface

steps.title: Stack and serve
steps.text: Brush lightly with ghee if you like and stack in a cloth-lined box to keep soft while you roll and cook the rest. Serve warm with dal and a sabzi.
steps.visual: A stack of soft, brown-spotted phulkas in a cloth-lined steel box, the top one glistening with a little ghee, a bowl of dal beside it

substitutions.note: Jowar rotis are gluten-free but need hot water to bind and are patted rather than rolled; they puff less.

recipes.storage: Wrap in a cloth inside a closed box and eat the same day. The dough keeps 1 day refrigerated.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a hot tawa for 10 seconds per side.

recipes.title: Bajra Roti (Pearl Millet Flatbread)
recipes.description: Rustic, earthy pearl-millet rotis from Rajasthan and Gujarat, patted out by hand and cooked on a tawa. Naturally gluten-free and best eaten hot. Makes 6 rotis; one serving = 2 rotis.

steps.title: Mix flour and salt
steps.text: Mix the bajra flour and salt in a wide bowl.
steps.visual: Grey-green bajra flour with a pinch of salt in a wide steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Knead in small batches
steps.text: Bajra has no gluten, so knead only enough for 2 rotis at a time. Take a third of the flour, add warm water a little at a time and knead with the heel of your palm for 2 to 3 minutes until smooth and free of cracks.
steps.visual: A smooth, soft grey dough ball being pressed with the heel of the palm on one side of the steel bowl, dry flour still heaped on the other side

steps.title: Pat out the rotis
steps.text: Divide into 2 balls. Dust with flour and pat each between your palms, or on a plastic sheet, into a 5-inch round about 3 mm thick. Smooth any cracking edges with a wet finger.
steps.visual: A round, slightly thick grey roti being patted out on a plastic sheet with wet fingertips, the edges smoothed

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium-high heat. Lay the roti on it and brush the top with a little water. Cook for about 1 minute until the underside has light spots.
steps.visual: A grey bajra roti on a black iron tawa, its top glistening with a thin film of water

steps.title: Flip and puff
steps.text: Flip, cook for 1 minute, then flip again and press gently with a folded cloth, or hold it over the flame, until it puffs in patches and has brown spots. Repeat with the remaining flour in batches.
steps.visual: A bajra roti over a gas flame, puffed in patches with dark brown spots across its surface

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Smear with a little ghee, if using, and serve hot with dal, a leafy sabzi or garlic chutney. Bajra rotis firm up as they cool.
steps.visual: Two hot, brown-spotted bajra rotis on a steel plate with a little ghee melting on top, a bowl of dal and a green sabzi beside them

substitutions.note: Jowar flour makes a softer, milder roti with the same method.

recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh; leftovers keep 1 day wrapped in a cloth.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a tawa with a sprinkle of water so they soften in the steam.

recipes.title: Soft Idli (Classic Fermented Batter)
recipes.description: Pillowy steamed idlis from a 4:1 idli rice and urad dal batter, ground and fermented overnight. Makes about 32 idlis; one serving = 4 idlis. Serve with sambar and chutney.

steps.title: Soak rice and dal
steps.text: Wash the idli rice 3 times and soak it in plenty of water in one bowl. In a second bowl wash the urad dal with the fenugreek seeds and soak them together. Soak both for 5 hours.
steps.visual: Two steel bowls on the counter: one of plump, opaque parboiled rice under water, the other of white split urad dal with a few yellow fenugreek seeds

steps.title: Grind the urad dal
steps.text: Drain the dal and grind it in a mixer or wet grinder, sprinkling in cold water a few tablespoons at a time, for 8 to 10 minutes until very smooth, fluffy and nearly doubled. A spoonful dropped into water should float.
steps.visual: Bright white, fluffy, mousse-like urad dal batter clinging to the sides of a mixer jar, a spoonful floating in a small cup of water beside it

steps.title: Grind the rice
steps.text: Transfer the dal batter to a large bowl. Drain the rice and grind it with just enough water to a slightly coarse batter, like fine semolina. Pour it over the dal batter.
steps.visual: A large steel mixing bowl of fluffy white dal batter with slightly grainy rice batter being poured over it from the mixer jar

steps.title: Mix with salt
steps.text: Add the salt and mix the two batters with your hand for a minute; the warmth of your hand helps fermentation. The batter should be thick but pourable.
steps.visual: A hand folding the combined thick, creamy-white idli batter in the large steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Ferment overnight
steps.text: Cover loosely and leave in a warm spot for 8 to 12 hours until the batter rises, looks bubbly and smells pleasantly sour. In cold weather, keep it inside a switched-off oven with the light on.
steps.visual: The same steel bowl the next morning, the batter risen almost to the rim with a domed surface full of tiny bubbles

steps.title: Grease the moulds
steps.text: Stir the batter gently without beating out the air. Grease the idli plates lightly with oil, pour 2 cups of water into the steamer or pressure-cooker base and bring it to a boil.
steps.visual: Lightly oiled steel idli plates stacked beside the bowl of bubbly batter, a pot of boiling water steaming behind them

steps.title: Fill and steam
steps.text: Fill each mould three-quarters full. Place the stand in the steamer, cover (remove the whistle if using a pressure cooker) and steam on medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
steps.visual: Idli moulds filled three-quarters with white batter on an idli stand being lowered into a steaming pot

steps.title: Rest and unmould
steps.text: Lift out the stand and leave it for 2 minutes, then run a wet spoon around each idli and lift it out.
steps.visual: Puffed, glossy white idlis in the steel idli plates, one being scooped out with a wet spoon

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with sambar and coconut or tomato chutney. Steam the remaining batter in batches as needed.
steps.visual: Four soft, round white idlis on a banana leaf with a cup of sambar and a spoonful of white coconut chutney

substitutions.note: Raw rice works but gives slightly firmer idlis; a handful of poha ground with the rice softens them.
Replace up to half the idli rice with foxtail millet soaked the same way; the idlis will be a little denser.

recipes.storage: Batter keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge and turns more sour. Cooked idlis keep 1 day refrigerated.
recipes.reheating: Steam for 3 to 4 minutes, or microwave covered with a damp cloth for 30 to 40 seconds.

recipes.title: Crisp Plain Dosa
recipes.description: Golden, paper-thin dosas from a thinner, rice-heavy batter of raw and parboiled rice with a little urad dal and chana dal for colour. Makes about 16 dosas; one serving = 2 dosas.

steps.title: Soak the grains
steps.text: Wash both rices together and soak them in one bowl. Wash the urad dal, chana dal and fenugreek together and soak them in another. Soak both for 5 hours.
steps.visual: Two steel bowls: one of white raw rice and opaque parboiled rice under water, the other of white urad dal, yellow chana dal and fenugreek seeds

steps.title: Grind the dals
steps.text: Drain the dals and grind with a little cold water for 5 to 6 minutes to a smooth, fluffy paste. Transfer to a large bowl.
steps.visual: Smooth, pale cream dal paste in a mixer jar, a spatula scraping down the sides

steps.title: Grind the rice smooth
steps.text: Grind the drained rice with water until completely smooth, finer than idli batter, with no grit when rubbed between your fingers. Add it to the dal paste.
steps.visual: Silky, smooth rice batter flowing from the mixer jar into the large steel mixing bowl of dal paste

steps.title: Salt and ferment
steps.text: Stir in the salt, mixing well by hand. Cover and ferment for 6 to 8 hours until bubbly and slightly risen. Dosa batter rises less than idli batter, and that is fine.
steps.visual: The large steel bowl of creamy batter with a bubbly, slightly risen surface after fermenting

steps.title: Thin the batter
steps.text: Stir the batter and add water a few spoons at a time until it flows like thick buttermilk and coats the back of a ladle thinly. Thinner batter gives crisper dosas.
steps.visual: A steel ladle lifted out of the thinned batter, a smooth, thin coating dripping off it back into the bowl

steps.title: Season the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron tawa on medium-high heat. Rub a few drops of oil over it with a folded cloth, then sprinkle a little water; it should sizzle off at once. Lower the heat to medium.
steps.visual: Water droplets sizzling and evaporating on a lightly oiled black cast-iron tawa

steps.title: Spread thin
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter into the centre and, using the back of the ladle, quickly spread it in outward spirals into a thin 9-inch crepe.
steps.visual: A thin, lacy circle of white batter being spread in spirals with the back of a ladle across the black tawa

steps.title: Crisp the dosa
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil around the edge and over the top. Cook for 1½ to 2 minutes without flipping until the underside is golden and the edges lift away from the tawa.
steps.visual: A thin dosa on the tawa turning golden-brown, the edges curling up and tiny oil bubbles on top

steps.title: Fold and serve
steps.text: Fold or roll the dosa and serve straight away with sambar and chutney. Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas and repeat with the remaining batter.
steps.visual: A crisp, golden rolled plain dosa on a steel plate with a cup of sambar and a spoonful of coconut chutney

substitutions.note: Ghee gives a richer, nuttier crust; use the same amount.
Leave out the chana dal if you don't have it; the dosas will be paler but still crisp.

recipes.storage: Batter keeps 3 days refrigerated; bring it to room temperature before cooking.
recipes.reheating: Dosas are best cooked fresh; warm leftovers briefly on a hot tawa.

recipes.title: Instant Oats Idli
recipes.description: No-ferment idlis of toasted, powdered oats with a little rava and curd, studded with carrot and a mustard–curry leaf tempering. Ready in about 40 minutes. Makes 16 idlis; one serving = 4 idlis.

steps.title: Toast and powder the oats
steps.text: Dry roast the oats in a kadai on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Cool for a few minutes, then grind to a fine powder in the mixer.
steps.visual: Lightly toasted oats in a black kadai, and beside it a mixer jar holding fine, pale oat powder

steps.title: Make the tempering
steps.text: Heat the oil in the same kadai on medium heat and add the mustard seeds. When they splutter, add the urad dal, chana dal and cashews (if using) and fry until golden, then add the curry leaves, green chilli and ginger for a few seconds.
steps.visual: Golden urad and chana dal, cashew pieces, crackling curry leaves and chopped green chilli in shimmering oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Roast the rava
steps.text: Add the rava to the tempering and roast on low heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty. Turn off the heat.
steps.visual: Pale rava coated in the tempering in the black kadai, dotted with mustard seeds and curry leaves

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Tip the rava mixture into a bowl with the oat powder, grated carrot, coriander and salt. Add the curd and water and mix to a thick, scoopable batter like idli batter.
steps.visual: Thick, speckled oat batter with orange carrot shreds and green coriander in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Rest the batter
steps.text: Cover and rest for 15 minutes so the oats and rava absorb the liquid. If it gets too stiff, stir in 1 to 2 tbsp water.
steps.visual: The same bowl of batter, now thicker and set, with a spoon standing upright in it

steps.title: Add soda and aerate
steps.text: Bring water to a boil in the steamer and grease the idli plates. Just before steaming, sprinkle the baking soda over the batter, pour 1 tsp water on it and fold gently until the batter turns light and airy.
steps.visual: Light, airy batter being folded in the steel bowl beside greased idli plates

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Fill the moulds and steam on medium heat for 12 minutes (no whistle on a pressure cooker) until a toothpick comes out clean.
steps.visual: An idli stand of filled moulds inside a steaming pot with the lid lifted, the oat idlis risen and set

steps.title: Unmould and serve
steps.text: Rest the idlis for 3 minutes, unmould with a wet spoon and serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.
steps.visual: Four golden-flecked oat idlis with visible carrot and coriander on a steel plate beside green coconut chutney and a cup of sambar

substitutions.note: Ragi flour in place of rava gives darker, earthier idlis; oats themselves may contain gluten unless labelled gluten-free.
If your curd is very sour, use half curd and half water so the idlis aren't too tangy.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; cooked idlis keep 1 day refrigerated. Don't store the batter once soda is added.
recipes.reheating: Steam for 3 to 4 minutes or microwave covered for 40 seconds.

recipes.title: Jeera Rice
recipes.description: Fragrant basmati rice cooked with cumin seeds toasted in ghee and a few whole spices, a simple base for dal, rajma and paneer curries. One serving = about 1 cup cooked (60 g raw).

steps.title: Rinse and soak
steps.text: Rinse the basmati gently 3 times until the water runs clear, then soak it in fresh water for 20 minutes. Drain well.
steps.visual: Long, slender basmati grains soaking in clear water in a steel bowl

steps.title: Toast the cumin
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy saucepan on medium heat. Add the bay leaves, cloves and cardamom, then the cumin seeds, and let them sizzle for about 30 seconds until they darken a shade.
steps.visual: Cumin seeds sizzling and browning in golden ghee with bay leaves, cloves and cardamom pods in a heavy steel saucepan

steps.title: Coat the rice
steps.text: Add the drained rice and stir gently for 1 to 2 minutes so every grain is coated in ghee.
steps.visual: Basmati grains glossy with ghee and flecked with cumin seeds in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Pour in the water, add the salt and bring to a boil.
steps.visual: Rice and whole spices under bubbling water in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the water is absorbed. In a pressure cooker, use 1½ cups water and cook for 1 whistle. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes.
steps.visual: The saucepan lid lifted to show cooked rice with small steam holes on its surface and cumin seeds on top

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Fluff with a fork, scatter over the coriander if using, and serve with dal tadka, rajma or a paneer curry.
steps.visual: Long, separate grains of jeera rice flecked with cumin and coriander in a white bowl, a bowl of yellow dal beside it

substitutions.note: Brown rice needs a 30-minute soak, 2½ cups water and 20 to 25 minutes of covered cooking.
Use oil to make it vegan.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and microwave covered, or warm in a covered pan on low heat.

recipes.title: Light Vegetable Quinoa Pulao
recipes.description: Quinoa cooked pulao-style with whole spices, mint, carrot, beans and peas in one pan. A light base for dal, kadhi or a chicken curry. One serving = about 1¼ cups.

steps.title: Rinse the quinoa
steps.text: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under running water for about a minute, rubbing it with your fingers to wash off its bitter coating. Drain well.
steps.visual: Small ivory quinoa seeds in a fine steel sieve under running water

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Slice the onion, slit the chilli, grate the ginger, dice the carrot, chop the beans and pick the mint leaves.
steps.visual: Sliced onion, diced carrot, chopped beans, green peas, a slit green chilli, grated ginger and mint leaves in separate piles on a wooden board

steps.title: Sizzle the whole spices
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy saucepan on medium heat. Add the cumin seeds, bay leaf, cloves and cinnamon and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
steps.visual: Cumin seeds, a bay leaf, cloves and a cinnamon stick sizzling in ghee in a heavy steel saucepan

steps.title: Sauté onion and vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion, green chilli and ginger and cook for 3 minutes until the onion softens. Add the carrot, beans and peas and sauté for 2 minutes more.
steps.visual: Softened onion with carrot cubes, beans and peas glistening among the whole spices in the steel saucepan

steps.title: Add quinoa and water
steps.text: Add the drained quinoa and stir with the vegetables for 1 minute. Pour in the water, add the salt and half the mint, and bring to a boil.
steps.visual: Quinoa and vegetables under bubbling water in the saucepan, a few mint leaves floating on top

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low heat for 13 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed and each grain shows a little white tail. In a pressure cooker, cook for 1 whistle. Rest covered for 5 minutes.
steps.visual: The lid lifted to show fluffy quinoa with visible curly white germ rings, studded with carrot and peas

steps.title: Fluff and serve
steps.text: Fluff with a fork, fold in the remaining mint and the lemon juice if using, and serve with dal, kadhi or a curry.
steps.visual: Fluffy vegetable quinoa pulao in a ceramic bowl with carrot, beans, peas and fresh mint on top

substitutions.note: Foxtail millet works with about 2¼ cups water per cup and 15 minutes of covered cooking.
Use oil to make it vegan.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; it packs well for lunch boxes.
recipes.reheating: Microwave covered with a splash of water for 1 to 2 minutes.

recipes.title: Cardamom–Banana Overnight Oats
recipes.description: No-cook oats soaked overnight in milk with chia seeds, cardamom and mashed banana, then topped with banana and almonds in the morning. Two jars take five minutes the night before.

steps.title: Mash the banana
steps.text: Mash half the banana in a bowl with a fork until smooth. Keep the other half for the topping.
steps.visual: Half a banana mashed to a pulp in a steel mixing bowl, the other half lying on a wooden board beside it

steps.title: Stir everything together
steps.text: Add the oats, milk, chia seeds and crushed cardamom to the mashed banana and stir well. Taste and add honey only if your banana isn't very ripe.
steps.visual: Rolled oats, black chia seeds and milk stirred together with mashed banana in the steel bowl, flecks of cardamom visible

steps.title: Divide into jars
steps.text: Spoon the mixture into two jars or lidded bowls.
steps.visual: Two glass jars each two-thirds filled with the milky oat and chia mixture, their lids lying beside them

steps.title: Chill overnight
steps.text: Close the jars and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight. The oats and chia soften and thicken without any cooking.
steps.visual: Two closed jars of thickened oats standing on a fridge shelf

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: In the morning, stir, loosen with a splash of milk if it is too thick, and top with the sliced banana and chopped almonds. Eat cold, or let it stand for 10 minutes to take the chill off.
steps.visual: An open jar of creamy overnight oats topped with banana coins and chopped almonds, a spoon resting in it

substitutions.note: Replace half the milk with curd for a tangier, thicker jar.
Walnuts or pumpkin seeds work just as well.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in closed jars in the fridge; add the banana and nuts just before eating.
recipes.reheating: Eat cold, or warm for 1 minute in the microwave with a splash of milk.

recipes.title: Vegetable Masala Oats
recipes.description: Savoury oats simmered into a soft, upma-like porridge with onion, tomato, carrot, peas, capsicum and a mustard–cumin tempering with crisp peanuts. A one-pan breakfast in 20 minutes.

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
steps.text: Chop the onion, tomato and capsicum, dice the carrot finely, chop the chilli and grate the ginger. Small pieces cook in the same time as the oats.
steps.visual: Small piles of chopped onion, tomato, capsicum, diced carrot, green peas, chopped green chilli and grated ginger on a wooden board

steps.title: Temper with peanuts
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai on medium heat. Add the mustard and cumin seeds and let them splutter, then add the curry leaves and peanuts and fry for 1 minute until the peanuts crisp.
steps.visual: Peanuts turning golden with spluttering mustard seeds, cumin and curry leaves in hot oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Add the onion, green chilli and ginger and sauté for 2 to 3 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.
steps.visual: Translucent chopped onion with green chilli and ginger among the peanuts in the black kadai

steps.title: Cook vegetables with spices
steps.text: Add the tomato, carrot, peas and capsicum with the turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala and salt. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
steps.visual: Softened tomato, orange carrot, green peas and capsicum coated in yellow-red spices in the kadai

steps.title: Simmer the oats
steps.text: Add the oats and stir for a minute, then pour in the water. Simmer on low heat, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until the oats are soft and the mixture is creamy but not gluey. Add a splash more water for a looser porridge.
steps.visual: Creamy, vegetable-studded oats bubbling gently in the kadai, a spoon drawn through the thick porridge

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat, stir in the coriander and lemon juice and serve hot.
steps.visual: A bowl of golden masala oats dotted with carrot, peas and peanuts, topped with fresh coriander

substitutions.note: Use pumpkin seeds for a peanut-free version; add them at the end so they stay green.

recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh; it thickens as it stands.
recipes.reheating: Loosen with hot water and warm on low heat, stirring.

recipes.title: Ragi Milk Kanji (Finger-Millet Porridge)
recipes.description: A smooth, warming porridge of ragi flour cooked in water and then milk, lightly sweetened with jaggery, scented with cardamom and topped with almonds. Ready in 15 minutes.

steps.title: Make a smooth slurry
steps.text: Whisk the ragi flour with 1 cup of cold water in a saucepan until completely smooth. Starting cold is what keeps the porridge lump-free.
steps.visual: A smooth, brownish-purple ragi slurry being whisked in a steel saucepan off the heat

steps.title: Cook the ragi
steps.text: Put the pan on medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, for 5 to 6 minutes until it thickens, turns glossy and darker, and no longer tastes raw.
steps.visual: Thick, glossy dark-brown ragi paste bubbling gently in the steel saucepan, a spoon drawn through it

steps.title: Add the milk
steps.text: Pour in the milk gradually, whisking, add the cardamom and simmer on low heat for 3 minutes until creamy.
steps.visual: Creamy, light-brown ragi porridge simmering in the saucepan, a whisk resting in it

steps.title: Sweeten off the heat
steps.text: Turn off the heat and stir in the jaggery until it dissolves. Adding jaggery off the heat keeps the milk from splitting.
steps.visual: Grated jaggery melting into the smooth ragi porridge in the saucepan on the switched-off stove

steps.title: Serve warm
steps.text: Pour into bowls or tumblers and scatter the chopped almonds on top. Add a little hot milk if it has thickened too much.
steps.visual: Two steel tumblers of smooth, warm ragi kanji with chopped almonds floating on top

substitutions.note: Blend 2 soft dates with a little milk instead; dates and jaggery are both sugars, so keep the amount small.
For a dairy-free kanji, use coconut milk diluted with water.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; it sets as it cools.
recipes.reheating: Whisk in hot milk or water and warm gently.

recipes.title: Oats & Vegetable Chilla
recipes.description: Thin savoury pancakes of powdered oats and curd, loaded with onion, tomato, carrot and capsicum and cooked on a tawa with very little oil. Makes 6 chillas; one serving = 3.

steps.title: Powder the oats
steps.text: Grind the oats to a fine flour in a dry mixer jar.
steps.visual: Fine, pale oat flour in a dry mixer jar with its lid off

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Tip the oat flour into a bowl and whisk in the curd, water, cumin, turmeric, chilli powder and salt to a smooth, pourable batter like thick dosa batter.
steps.visual: Smooth, pale-yellow oat batter flecked with cumin being whisked in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Fold in the vegetables
steps.text: Stir in the onion, tomato, carrot, capsicum, green chilli, ginger and coriander.
steps.visual: The oat batter in the steel bowl now speckled with chopped onion, red tomato, orange carrot, green capsicum and coriander

steps.title: Rest the batter
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes; the oats will thicken the batter. If it becomes too thick to spread, stir in 1 to 2 tbsp water.
steps.visual: The vegetable-studded batter, now thicker, resting in the steel bowl with a ladle in it

steps.title: Spread on the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium heat and smear it with a few drops of oil. Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a 6-inch round about 3 mm thick.
steps.visual: A round of vegetable-studded oat batter spread on a lightly oiled black tawa, a ladle beside it

steps.title: Cook both sides
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil around the edge and cook for 2 minutes until the underside is golden and the top looks set. Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
steps.visual: A flipped chilla on the tawa showing a golden-brown surface with charred vegetable flecks

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Serve the chillas hot with green chutney or a small bowl of curd.
steps.visual: Three golden oats chillas folded on a steel plate with a small bowl of green chutney beside them

substitutions.note: For a dairy-free chilla, use all water plus a squeeze of lemon.
Swap a third of the oat flour for ragi flour for an earthier taste.

recipes.storage: Batter keeps 1 day refrigerated; it thickens, so thin it with water before cooking.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a hot tawa for 30 seconds per side.

recipes.title: Sprouted Moong Poha
recipes.description: Thick poha tossed with lightly steamed moong sprouts, grated carrot and a curry-leaf tempering, finished with lemon and coriander. More crunch and protein than plain poha, in 20 minutes.

steps.title: Steam the sprouts
steps.text: Simmer the sprouts in a little salted water in a small saucepan for 4 to 5 minutes until just tender but still crunchy. Drain.
steps.visual: Moong sprouts with little white tails in a small steel saucepan of simmering water

steps.title: Rinse the poha
steps.text: Put the poha in a sieve and rinse under running water for 15 to 20 seconds, tossing, until just soft. Drain and leave for 5 minutes to fluff up.
steps.visual: Damp, softened white poha flakes in a steel sieve, plump but still separate

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai on medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and when they splutter add the curry leaves and green chilli.
steps.visual: Spluttering mustard seeds, crackling curry leaves and green chilli pieces in hot oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Cook onion and carrot
steps.text: Add the onion and cook for 2 minutes until soft, then add the carrot and turmeric and stir for 1 minute.
steps.visual: Soft onion and orange carrot shreds turning yellow with turmeric in the kadai

steps.title: Toss in poha and sprouts
steps.text: Add the poha, sprouts and salt. Toss gently on low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until hot through, without mashing the flakes.
steps.visual: Yellow poha flakes tossed with green moong sprouts, carrot and curry leaves in the kadai

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat, squeeze over the lemon juice and fold in the coriander. Serve topped with grated coconut if you like.
steps.visual: A plate of yellow sprouted moong poha topped with coriander and white grated coconut, a lemon wedge on the side

substitutions.note: Sprouted black chana works too; pressure cook it for 2 whistles first.

recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh; poha hardens in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and microwave covered for 1 minute.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter–Banana Whole-Wheat Toast
recipes.description: Crisp whole-wheat toast spread with unsweetened peanut butter and layered with banana, cinnamon and crushed flax seeds. A five-minute breakfast that children enjoy too.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Toast the bread slices on a dry tawa over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until crisp and golden, or use a toaster.
steps.visual: Four slices of whole-wheat bread browning on a dry black tawa

steps.title: Slice the banana
steps.text: Peel the banana and cut it into thin coins.
steps.visual: Thin banana coins fanned out on a wooden board beside the peel

steps.title: Spread the peanut butter
steps.text: Spread the peanut butter over the warm toast so it softens slightly.
steps.visual: Four golden toast slices on a board, each spread with a glossy layer of peanut butter

steps.title: Layer and sprinkle
steps.text: Arrange the banana slices over the peanut butter, then sprinkle with cinnamon and crushed flax seeds. Drizzle with honey only if you want it sweeter.
steps.visual: Toast slices covered in overlapping banana coins, dusted with cinnamon and speckled with crushed flax seeds

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cut each slice in half and serve straight away while the toast is still crisp.
steps.visual: Peanut butter–banana toast halves on a white plate, banana coins and flax visible, a glass of milk behind

substitutions.note: Use tahini for a peanut-free version.
Choose bread that lists whole-wheat flour as the first ingredient; many brown breads are mostly refined flour.

recipes.title: Boiled Egg & Vegetable Whole-Wheat Sandwich
recipes.description: Chopped boiled eggs bound with peppery hung curd, layered with cucumber, tomato and onion between toasted whole-wheat bread. Filling, portable and ready in about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 10 minutes for firm yolks, then cool them in cold water and peel.
steps.visual: Four white eggs in bubbling water in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Make the egg filling
steps.text: Chop the eggs and mix them in a bowl with the hung curd, crushed pepper, salt, onion, green chilli and coriander.
steps.visual: Chopped boiled egg with white and yellow pieces bound in thick curd, flecked with black pepper, onion and coriander in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Slice the vegetables
steps.text: Slice the cucumber and tomato thinly and pat the tomato dry so the bread doesn't go soggy.
steps.visual: Thin rounds of cucumber and tomato laid out on a wooden board

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Toast the bread on a dry tawa over medium heat for about 1 minute per side until crisp.
steps.visual: Four whole-wheat bread slices turning golden on a black tawa

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spread a little mustard on two slices if you like. Pile on the egg filling, layer cucumber and tomato on top and close with the remaining slices. Press gently and cut diagonally.
steps.visual: An open sandwich on the board with a thick layer of egg filling topped with cucumber and tomato rounds, the top slice being placed

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve straight away, or wrap tightly in butter paper for a lunch box.
steps.visual: Two diagonally cut whole-wheat sandwiches on a plate, showing layers of egg filling, cucumber and tomato

substitutions.note: Mayonnaise is the classic binder but adds far more fat per spoon than hung curd.
Crumbled paneer makes a vegetarian version.

recipes.storage: Keep the egg filling separate and assemble before eating; the filling keeps 1 day refrigerated.

recipes.title: Fruit, Nut & Curd Breakfast Bowl
recipes.description: Thick, cinnamon-dusted curd topped with banana, apple, papaya, pomegranate, almonds, walnuts and pumpkin seeds. No cooking, ready in 10 minutes and easy to vary with seasonal fruit.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Whisk the chilled curd with the cinnamon in a bowl until smooth and creamy.
steps.visual: Smooth white curd with a light dusting of cinnamon being whisked in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Cut the fruit
steps.text: Slice the banana, dice the apple and cube the papaya into bite-sized pieces. Cut the apple last so it doesn't brown.
steps.visual: Banana coins, apple dice, orange papaya cubes and ruby pomegranate arils in small heaps on a wooden board

steps.title: Chop the nuts
steps.text: Roughly chop the almonds and break the walnuts into small pieces.
steps.visual: Chopped almonds, walnut pieces and green pumpkin seeds on the corner of the wooden board

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.text: Divide the curd between two bowls. Arrange the fruit on top in sections and scatter over the nuts and seeds.
steps.visual: Two bowls of white curd topped with neat sections of banana, apple, papaya and pomegranate, sprinkled with nuts and seeds

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Drizzle with honey only if you want it sweeter, and eat straight away.
steps.visual: A colourful fruit, nut and curd bowl with a spoon dipped in, a thin thread of honey on top

substitutions.note: Hung curd makes a thicker bowl with about three times the protein.
Use mango in summer.

recipes.storage: Assemble just before eating; cut apple browns and nuts soften on standing.

recipes.title: Banana–Oat Pancakes
recipes.description: Soft, naturally sweet pancakes blended from oats, ripe banana, eggs and milk, with no refined flour or added sugar in the batter. Makes 8 small pancakes; one serving = 4.

steps.title: Blend the batter
steps.text: Put the oats, peeled banana, eggs, milk, cinnamon and salt in a blender and blend for 30 to 40 seconds until smooth.
steps.visual: A blender jar of smooth, thick, pale-beige banana-oat batter

steps.title: Add baking powder and rest
steps.text: Stir in the baking powder and leave the batter for 5 minutes to thicken slightly.
steps.visual: The thick batter in the blender jar with small air bubbles rising to the surface

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick pan on medium-low heat and brush it with a little ghee.
steps.visual: A thin sheen of melted ghee brushed over a non-stick pan on a low flame

steps.title: Cook the pancakes
steps.text: Pour 3 tbsp of batter per pancake, keeping them small so they are easy to flip. Cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the edges set, flip and cook 1 minute more. Banana batter browns quickly, so keep the heat gentle. Repeat with the rest.
steps.visual: Three small round pancakes in the pan, one flipped to show an even golden-brown surface, bubbles on the others

steps.title: Serve warm
steps.text: Stack and serve warm with sliced fruit, a spoon of curd, or a little honey if you like.
steps.visual: A stack of four golden banana-oat pancakes on a plate with banana slices and a thin drizzle of honey

substitutions.note: For eggless pancakes, soak 2 tbsp chia seeds in 6 tbsp water for 10 minutes; they will be softer.
Any neutral oil works for greasing the pan.

recipes.storage: Cooked pancakes keep 2 days refrigerated.
recipes.reheating: Warm in a pan for 30 seconds per side.

recipes.title: Vegetable Quinoa Upma
recipes.description: South Indian–style upma made with quinoa in place of rava, tempered with mustard, urad dal, curry leaves and cashews and packed with carrot, beans and peas. Ready in about 25 minutes.

steps.title: Rinse the quinoa
steps.text: Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under running water for a minute, rubbing it to remove the bitter coating. Drain well.
steps.visual: Ivory quinoa seeds in a fine steel sieve under a stream of running water

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadai on medium heat. Add the mustard seeds; once they splutter, add the urad dal, chana dal and cashews and fry until golden. Add the curry leaves, green chilli and ginger.
steps.visual: Golden urad dal, chana dal and cashews with spluttering mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli and ginger in a black kadai

steps.title: Sauté the vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion and cook for 2 minutes until soft, then add the carrot, beans and peas and sauté for 2 minutes.
steps.visual: Soft onion, diced carrot, chopped beans and peas glistening in the tempering in the kadai

steps.title: Add water and quinoa
steps.text: Pour in the water, add the salt and bring to a boil. Stir in the drained quinoa.
steps.visual: Quinoa and vegetables in bubbling water in the kadai, curry leaves floating on top

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the quinoa is tender with visible white tails. Rest covered for 3 minutes.
steps.visual: The lid lifted off the kadai to show fluffy, cooked quinoa upma with carrot, beans and peas

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Fluff with a fork, add the lemon juice, coriander and ghee if using, and serve hot with coconut chutney.
steps.visual: A mound of vegetable quinoa upma on a steel plate with cashews and curry leaves on top and coconut chutney beside it

substitutions.note: Foxtail millet makes an equally good upma; use 2½ cups water per cup and cook for 15 minutes.
Peanuts are cheaper and just as crunchy.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and microwave covered, or warm in a pan.

recipes.title: Egg-White & Vegetable Omelette Roll
recipes.description: A thin whole-wheat roti cooked onto a fluffy egg-white and spinach omelette, then rolled Kolkata-style around lemony onion, tomato and capsicum. Makes 2 rolls; one serving = 1 roll.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the atta with a pinch of the salt and the water and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
steps.visual: A small ball of soft whole-wheat dough in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Rest dough, prep filling
steps.text: Cover the dough and rest it for 15 minutes. Meanwhile toss the sliced onion, tomato and capsicum with the lemon juice and chaat masala.
steps.visual: The covered dough bowl in the background; in front, a plate of sliced onion, tomato and capsicum strips glistening with lemon and dusted with chaat masala

steps.title: Whisk the eggs
steps.text: Whisk the egg whites with the whole egg, spinach, green chilli, pepper, coriander and the remaining salt until frothy.
steps.visual: Frothy egg whites flecked with chopped spinach, green chilli and coriander in a steel bowl with a whisk

steps.title: Half-cook the rotis
steps.text: Divide the dough in two and roll each into a thin 8-inch roti. Cook each on a hot tawa for about 30 seconds per side until just set but still pale.
steps.visual: A thin, pale, half-cooked roti on a black tawa with faint light spots

steps.title: Cook omelette onto the roti
steps.text: Drizzle 1 tsp oil on the tawa and pour in half the egg mixture, tilting so it spreads to the size of the roti. Immediately lay a roti on top and press. Cook for 1½ minutes until the egg sets, flip and cook the roti side for 1 minute with a few drops of oil until golden. Repeat.
steps.visual: A roti pressed onto a set, spinach-flecked egg-white omelette on the tawa, the edges turning lightly golden

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.text: Slide each one onto a board, egg side up. Spread half the onion-tomato filling along one edge and roll up tightly.
steps.visual: A golden roti with the green-flecked omelette facing up, sliced onion, tomato and capsicum lined along one edge, half rolled

steps.title: Wrap and serve
steps.text: Wrap the bottom half of each roll in butter paper and serve warm with green chutney.
steps.visual: Two egg-white omelette rolls wrapped in butter paper on a plate, onion and capsicum peeking from the open ends, a small bowl of green chutney beside

substitutions.note: Use 3 more whole eggs in place of the whites for a richer roll with more fat.
Finely chopped methi leaves add a pleasant bitterness.

recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh; the rolls turn soggy on standing.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a dry tawa for 1 minute per side.

recipes.title: Boiled Egg & Moong Sprout Chaat Salad
recipes.description: Lightly steamed moong sprouts tossed with chopped boiled eggs, cucumber, tomato, onion and roasted peanuts, sharpened with lemon and chaat masala. A filling breakfast or light lunch with lots of crunch.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Cover the eggs with cold water in a saucepan, bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Cool in cold water, peel and cut into quarters.
steps.visual: Four eggs simmering in a steel saucepan of bubbling water

steps.title: Steam the sprouts
steps.text: In the same saucepan, simmer the sprouts in a little salted water for 3 to 4 minutes until just tender but still crunchy. Drain and cool.
steps.visual: Green moong sprouts with white tails being drained in a steel sieve over the saucepan

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
steps.text: Chop the cucumber, tomato, onion, green chilli and coriander.
steps.visual: Chopped cucumber, tomato, onion, green chilli and coriander in heaps on a wooden board, the peeled egg quarters on a plate beside

steps.title: Toss the chaat
steps.text: In a large bowl, toss the sprouts and chopped vegetables with the peanuts, lemon juice, chaat masala, pepper and salt.
steps.visual: Moong sprouts, cucumber, tomato and peanuts tossed with chaat masala in a wide steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Fold in the egg quarters gently so the yolks stay whole.
steps.visual: Boiled egg quarters with bright yellow yolks resting on top of the sprout chaat in the steel bowl

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve straight away, with an extra squeeze of lemon if you like.
steps.visual: A bowl of moong sprout chaat salad topped with boiled egg quarters, peanuts and coriander, a lemon wedge on the rim

substitutions.note: Cubed paneer makes it vegetarian.
Roasted gram is a peanut-free crunch.

recipes.storage: Eat within 2 hours of dressing. Undressed sprouts, chopped vegetables and peeled eggs keep 1 day refrigerated, stored separately.

recipes.title: Paneer–Vegetable Whole-Wheat Frankie
recipes.description: Mumbai-style frankie rolls: soft whole-wheat rotis wrapped around spiced, pan-seared paneer, onion, capsicum and cabbage with a mint–curd chutney. Makes 2 large wraps; one serving = 1 wrap.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the atta, a pinch of the salt and the water and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
steps.visual: A soft, smooth ball of whole-wheat dough in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Rest dough, blend chutney
steps.text: Cover the dough and rest it for 15 minutes. Meanwhile blend the hung curd with the mint, coriander, green chilli, lemon juice and a pinch of salt into a thick green chutney.
steps.visual: The covered dough bowl behind a small mixer jar of thick, pale-green mint and curd chutney

steps.title: Spice the paneer
steps.text: Toss the paneer fingers with the Kashmiri chilli, garam masala, half the chaat masala and a pinch of salt.
steps.visual: Paneer fingers coated in red-orange spices on a steel plate

steps.title: Cook the rotis
steps.text: Divide the dough in two and roll each into a thin 9-inch roti. Cook on a hot tawa for 40 seconds per side until light brown spots appear, then keep wrapped in a cloth.
steps.visual: A large, thin whole-wheat roti with light brown spots on a black tawa

steps.title: Sear paneer and vegetables
steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan on medium heat and cook the paneer for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until golden in spots. Push it aside, add the onion and capsicum and toss on high heat for 2 minutes so they stay crunchy.
steps.visual: Golden, spice-coated paneer fingers beside crisp onion and green capsicum strips in a non-stick pan

steps.title: Assemble the frankies
steps.text: Spread the chutney over each roti, line shredded cabbage down the middle, pile on the paneer and vegetables and sprinkle with the rest of the chaat masala. Fold in the bottom and roll up tightly.
steps.visual: A roti spread with green chutney, topped with shredded cabbage, seared paneer, onion and capsicum, its bottom edge folded up

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Wrap the lower half of each frankie in butter paper and serve warm.
steps.visual: Two paneer frankies wrapped in butter paper, cut on the diagonal to show the paneer and vegetable filling

substitutions.note: Use pressed firm tofu, and thick plant yoghurt in the chutney, to make it vegan.
Regular curd makes a runnier chutney; use less so the wrap doesn't go soggy.

recipes.storage: For lunch boxes, pack rotis, filling and chutney separately; they keep 1 day refrigerated.
recipes.reheating: Warm the filling in a pan and the rotis on a tawa before rolling.

recipes.title: Roasted Chana & Peanut Snack Mix
recipes.description: A crunchy jar snack of roasted gram, peanuts and pumpkin seeds tossed in a teaspoon of oil with crisp curry leaves, turmeric, chilli and hing. Makes 6 small bowls of about 30 g each.

steps.title: Roast the peanuts
steps.text: Dry roast the peanuts in a kadai on low heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until they crackle and the skins blister. Rub off the loose skins if you like.
steps.visual: Peanuts with blistered, darkening skins being stirred in a dry black kadai

steps.title: Crisp the gram and seeds
steps.text: Add the roasted gram and pumpkin seeds and stir for 2 to 3 minutes until warm and crisp. Tip everything onto a plate.
steps.visual: Pale-yellow roasted gram, green pumpkin seeds and brown peanuts mixed together in the kadai

steps.title: Fry the curry leaves
steps.text: Heat the oil in the same kadai on medium heat and fry the curry leaves for about 30 seconds until crisp. Turn off the heat and stir in the hing, turmeric and chilli powder.
steps.visual: Crisp, dark-green curry leaves in a little oil tinted red and yellow with chilli and turmeric in the kadai

steps.title: Toss to coat
steps.text: Return the nuts and gram to the kadai with the salt and toss well off the heat until everything is evenly coated with the spices.
steps.visual: Peanuts, roasted gram and pumpkin seeds coated in red-orange spice and flecked with crisp curry leaves in the kadai

steps.title: Cool and serve
steps.text: Cool completely before storing in an airtight jar. Serve a small bowl, about 30 g, with tea.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of spiced chana and peanut mix with curry leaves beside a glass jar of more and a cup of tea

substitutions.note: Use almonds for a peanut-free mix; it costs more.
Most compounded hing contains wheat flour; leave it out or use a gluten-free brand if needed.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight jar.

recipes.title: Roasted Masala Makhana
recipes.description: Fox nuts slow-roasted until they snap, then tossed in a little spiced ghee with turmeric, chilli, black pepper and chaat masala. A light, crunchy tea-time snack that keeps for a week.

steps.title: Dry roast the makhana
steps.text: Roast the makhana in a dry kadai on low heat for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until one crushed between your fingers snaps cleanly. In an air fryer, cook at 150°C for 8 minutes, shaking twice.
steps.visual: Puffy white makhana being stirred in a dry black kadai over a low flame

steps.title: Make the spiced ghee
steps.text: Push the makhana to the side, melt the ghee in the centre of the kadai and stir in the turmeric, chilli powder and pepper for about 10 seconds.
steps.visual: A small pool of golden ghee tinted with turmeric and chilli in the middle of the kadai, crisp makhana pushed to the sides

steps.title: Toss with masala
steps.text: Toss the makhana through the spiced ghee for 1 to 2 minutes, then turn off the heat and sprinkle over the chaat masala and salt. Toss again.
steps.visual: Makhana evenly coated in a light orange spice dusting in the kadai

steps.title: Cool to crisp
steps.text: Spread on a plate and cool for 10 minutes; the makhana gets crunchier as it cools.
steps.visual: Spiced makhana spread out in a single layer on a steel plate, cooling

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve a cupful as a tea-time snack and store the rest airtight.
steps.visual: A small bowl of orange-dusted masala makhana beside a cup of masala chai

substitutions.note: Use oil to make it vegan.

recipes.storage: Cool fully and store in an airtight jar for up to a week.

recipes.title: Masala Fruit Chaat
recipes.description: Apple, papaya, guava, banana, orange and pomegranate tossed with lemon juice, chaat masala, roasted cumin, black salt and mint. Sweet, tangy and ready in 10 minutes.

steps.title: Cut the firm fruit
steps.text: Wash the fruit. Dice the apple and guava, cube the papaya and peel and segment the orange into bite-sized pieces.
steps.visual: Diced red apple, pale-green guava, orange papaya cubes and orange segments in heaps on a wooden board

steps.title: Add banana and pomegranate
steps.text: Tip the cut fruit into a wide bowl, slice in the banana and scatter over the pomegranate arils.
steps.visual: Mixed cut fruit in a wide steel bowl with banana coins and ruby pomegranate arils on top

steps.title: Dress the fruit
steps.text: Squeeze over the lemon juice and sprinkle with chaat masala, roasted cumin and black salt. Toss gently so the banana doesn't break.
steps.visual: Glistening fruit in the steel bowl dusted with brown chaat masala and cumin, a spoon tossing it

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fold in the shredded mint and serve straight away.
steps.visual: Masala fruit chaat in small bowls, the colourful fruit flecked with spice and topped with fresh mint leaves

substitutions.note: In summer, use mango in place of papaya.
If guava is out of season, double the pomegranate.

recipes.storage: Best eaten within 30 minutes; banana and apple brown on standing.

recipes.title: Moong Sprouts Chaat
recipes.description: Crunchy, lightly steamed moong sprouts with onion, tomato, cucumber, pomegranate and roasted gram, sharpened with lemon, chaat masala, roasted cumin and green chilli.

steps.title: Steam the sprouts
steps.text: Simmer the sprouts in a little water in a covered saucepan for 3 to 4 minutes until they lose their raw taste but still crunch. Drain and spread out to cool.
steps.visual: Bright green moong sprouts with white tails steaming in a small covered steel saucepan, the lid lifted

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, tomato, cucumber, green chilli and coriander.
steps.visual: Neat piles of chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, green chilli and coriander on a wooden board

steps.title: Toss together
steps.text: In a bowl, toss the cooled sprouts with the chopped vegetables, pomegranate, roasted gram, lemon juice, chaat masala, cumin and salt.
steps.visual: Moong sprouts, chopped vegetables, pomegranate arils and roasted gram being tossed with spices in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve straight away so the vegetables stay crisp.
steps.visual: A bowl of colourful moong sprouts chaat with red pomegranate, green coriander and a lemon wedge on top

substitutions.note: Roasted peanuts give a richer crunch.
Eat raw sprouts only if very fresh; the short steaming makes them easier to digest and safer.

recipes.storage: Dress just before eating. Plain steamed sprouts keep 2 days refrigerated.

recipes.title: Ragi–Oats Jaggery Cookies
recipes.description: Crisp, nutty cookies of ragi flour, oats and whole-wheat flour, sweetened with a modest amount of jaggery and scented with cardamom. Makes 16 cookies; one serving = 2.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 170°C and line a baking tray with parchment.
steps.visual: A parchment-lined baking tray in front of an oven with its dial set to 170°C

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the ragi flour, oats, atta, baking powder, baking soda, cardamom and salt.
steps.visual: Reddish-brown ragi flour, rolled oats and wheat flour stirred together in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Cream butter and jaggery
steps.text: In a second bowl, beat the soft butter and powdered jaggery with a whisk for 2 to 3 minutes until creamy and slightly paler.
steps.visual: Creamy, caramel-coloured butter and jaggery mixture being beaten with a whisk in a glass bowl

steps.title: Bring the dough together
steps.text: Add the dry mixture and the almonds, if using, to the creamed butter and fold together. Add the milk a spoonful at a time until the dough just holds when pressed.
steps.visual: A soft, crumbly dark-brown cookie dough pressed together in the glass bowl, flecked with oats and chopped almonds

steps.title: Shape the cookies
steps.text: Roll into 16 balls and flatten each to about 5 mm thick on the tray, leaving 2 cm between them. Smooth any cracked edges.
steps.visual: Sixteen flattened round cookie discs in neat rows on the parchment-lined baking tray

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake at 170°C for 15 to 18 minutes until the edges are firm and the kitchen smells toasty. Ragi is dark, so judge doneness by firmness, not colour.
steps.visual: Baked ragi-oat cookies on the tray inside a lit oven, slightly risen with firm, dry edges

steps.title: Cool on the tray
steps.text: Leave on the tray for 15 minutes; the cookies are soft when hot and crisp up as they cool.
steps.visual: The baking tray of cookies cooling on the counter, a few small cracks across their tops

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve two cookies with tea or milk and store the rest airtight.
steps.visual: Two dark, crisp ragi-oat cookies on a saucer beside a cup of tea, one broken to show the oat-flecked inside

substitutions.note: Jaggery is still sugar, nutritionally close to white sugar. You can cut it to 40 g; the cookies will be less sweet and a little crumblier.
Melted ghee works; the cookies spread less and taste nuttier.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 week in an airtight tin.

recipes.title: Savoury Moong Dal Steamed Muffins
recipes.description: Soft, spongy savoury muffins of soaked and ground yellow moong dal with carrot and spinach, steamed in small cups and topped with a mustard–sesame tempering. Makes 12; one serving = 3.

ingredients.prep: half for greasing, half for tempering

steps.title: Soak the dal
steps.text: Wash the moong dal 2 to 3 times and soak it in plenty of water for 2 hours.
steps.visual: Yellow split moong dal soaking under clear water in a steel bowl

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Drain the dal and grind it with the green chilli, ginger and only as much water as needed into a thick, slightly coarse batter.
steps.visual: Thick, pale-yellow moong dal batter in a mixer jar, a spatula scraping it down

steps.title: Add curd and vegetables
steps.text: Transfer the batter to a bowl and stir in the curd, carrot, spinach, turmeric, hing and salt.
steps.visual: Yellow batter speckled with orange carrot and green spinach in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Prepare the cups
steps.text: Bring water to a boil in a steamer or pressure cooker. Grease 12 small steel katoris or silicone muffin cups with half the oil.
steps.visual: Twelve small, lightly oiled steel katoris arranged on a steamer plate beside the bowl of batter

steps.title: Aerate and fill
steps.text: Sprinkle the baking soda over the batter, pour 1 tsp water on top of it and fold gently until the batter turns light and fluffy. Fill each cup three-quarters full.
steps.visual: Fluffy, aerated vegetable batter being spooned into the greased steel katoris

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium heat for 15 minutes (without the whistle in a pressure cooker) until risen and a toothpick comes out clean. Rest 5 minutes, then unmould.
steps.visual: Risen, spongy yellow muffins in steel katoris inside an open steamer, steam curling up

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in a small kadai, add the mustard seeds and when they splutter add the sesame seeds and curry leaves for a few seconds.
steps.visual: Popping mustard seeds, golden sesame and crackling curry leaves in a little oil in a small kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the tempering over the unmoulded muffins, scatter with coriander and serve warm with green chutney.
steps.visual: Three golden moong dal muffins on a plate topped with mustard seeds, sesame and curry leaves, a small bowl of green chutney beside

substitutions.note: Red lentils work with a 1½-hour soak; the muffins turn salmon-orange.
For dairy-free muffins, use 2 tsp lemon juice plus 3 tbsp water in place of the curd.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Steam for 3 to 4 minutes or microwave covered for 30 seconds.

recipes.title: Baked Sweet Potato Chaat
recipes.description: Sweet potato cubes roasted until caramelised at the edges, then tossed with lemon, chaat masala, onion and pomegranate and finished with mint-flecked hung curd.

steps.title: Preheat and cube
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Scrub the sweet potatoes, leave the skin on and cut them into 2 cm cubes.
steps.visual: Even 2 cm cubes of orange-fleshed sweet potato with purple skin on a wooden board

steps.title: Season the cubes
steps.text: Toss the cubes in a bowl with the oil, cumin powder, chilli powder and a pinch of salt.
steps.visual: Sweet potato cubes glossy with oil and dusted with red-brown spices in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Spread in a single layer on a baking tray and roast at 200°C for 25 to 28 minutes, turning halfway, until tender with caramelised edges. In an air fryer, cook at 190°C for 15 to 18 minutes, shaking twice.
steps.visual: Roasted sweet potato cubes with dark caramelised edges on a baking tray straight out of the oven

steps.title: Make the mint curd
steps.text: Whisk the hung curd with the mint, a pinch of salt and 1 tbsp water until smooth and drizzly.
steps.visual: Smooth white hung curd flecked with green mint in a small bowl with a spoon

steps.title: Toss the chaat
steps.text: Tip the hot sweet potato into the bowl and toss with the onion, pomegranate, lemon juice, chaat masala and coriander.
steps.visual: Caramelised sweet potato cubes tossed with chopped onion, pomegranate arils and coriander in the steel bowl

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile onto plates, drizzle with the mint curd and serve warm.
steps.visual: A plate of sweet potato chaat drizzled with white mint curd, red pomegranate arils and green coriander on top

substitutions.note: Regular potato works but is less sweet and needs 5 more minutes.
Plain curd makes a thinner drizzle; skip the water.

recipes.storage: Roasted cubes keep 2 days refrigerated; add the toppings just before serving.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp the cubes in an air fryer at 180°C for 4 minutes.

recipes.title: Sesame–Peanut Date Energy Bites
recipes.description: No-bake bites of roasted peanuts, toasted sesame and oats bound with soft dates and cardamom, then rolled in coconut. Makes 16 bites; one serving = 2.

steps.title: Roast the peanuts
steps.text: Dry roast the peanuts in a kadai on low heat for 5 minutes until fragrant and lightly browned. Tip out and rub off the skins.
steps.visual: Golden roasted peanuts with flaking skins in a dry black kadai

steps.title: Toast sesame and oats
steps.text: In the same kadai, toast the sesame seeds and oats on low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the sesame turns pale gold and starts to pop.
steps.visual: Pale-gold sesame seeds and rolled oats being stirred in the kadai

steps.title: Grind coarsely
steps.text: Cool for 5 minutes, then pulse the peanuts, sesame, oats and cardamom in the mixer to a coarse, sandy crumb.
steps.visual: A coarse, sandy crumb of ground peanuts, sesame and oats in a mixer jar

steps.title: Add the dates
steps.text: Add the seeded dates and pulse until the mixture clumps together into a sticky dough.
steps.visual: A sticky brown dough of dates and peanut crumb clumped around the mixer blade

steps.title: Shape the bites
steps.text: With lightly damp hands, roll the mixture into 16 walnut-sized balls.
steps.visual: Sixteen glossy brown date-and-peanut balls lined up on a steel plate

steps.title: Roll in coconut
steps.text: Roll each ball in desiccated coconut to coat.
steps.visual: Brown energy bites being rolled in a shallow bowl of white desiccated coconut

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve two bites as a snack and store the rest in an airtight box.
steps.visual: Coconut-coated sesame–peanut energy bites in a small bowl, one cut in half to show the speckled inside

substitutions.note: Use almonds for a peanut-free version.
If your dates are dry, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes and drain well before blending.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 week in an airtight box, or 3 weeks in the fridge.

recipes.title: Ragi Jaggery Ladoo
recipes.description: Small, fudgy ladoos of ghee-roasted ragi flour, ground peanuts and jaggery, scented with cardamom. Portioned at one ladoo per serving; makes 12.

steps.title: Roast the peanuts
steps.text: Dry roast the peanuts in a kadai on low heat for 5 minutes until crisp. Cool and rub off the skins.
steps.visual: Roasted peanuts with loosened skins in a dry black kadai

steps.title: Grind with jaggery
steps.text: Pulse the peanuts with the jaggery and cardamom in the mixer to a fine, slightly moist powder.
steps.visual: Fine, golden-brown peanut and jaggery powder in a mixer jar

steps.title: Roast ragi in ghee
steps.text: Warm two-thirds of the ghee in the kadai, add the ragi flour and roast on low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty and turns a shade darker.
steps.visual: Dark reddish-brown ragi flour being stirred with ghee in the kadai, looking like damp sand

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Turn off the heat. Add the peanut–jaggery powder and the remaining ghee and mix thoroughly while the flour is warm, so the jaggery softens and binds.
steps.visual: Ragi flour and peanut–jaggery powder mixed into an even, moist brown crumb in the kadai

steps.title: Shape while warm
steps.text: While still warm, take about 2 tablespoons of the mixture and press it firmly into a ball. If it won't hold, sprinkle in a little warm milk. Make 12 ladoos.
steps.visual: A hand pressing warm ragi mixture into a firm round ladoo, a few finished ladoos on a steel plate

steps.title: Cool to set
steps.text: Leave the ladoos for 10 minutes to firm up.
steps.visual: Twelve dark-brown ragi ladoos cooling in rows on a steel plate

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve one ladoo as a sweet after a meal or with tea.
steps.visual: One ragi ladoo on a small brass plate beside a cup of tea, its surface showing flecks of peanut

substitutions.note: Jaggery is sugar, nutritionally close to white sugar. Ground soft dates sweeten with a little fibre but are also high in sugar.

recipes.storage: Keeps 10 days in an airtight box at room temperature.

recipes.title: Date & Nut Ladoo
recipes.description: Soft ladoos of dates cooked down with a little ghee and studded with toasted almonds, cashews, walnuts and pistachios. Sweetened only by the dates; makes 12, one per serving.

steps.title: Toast the nuts
steps.text: Dry roast the almonds, cashews, walnuts and pistachios in a kadai on low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until fragrant. Tip onto a plate to cool.
steps.visual: Almonds, cashews, walnut halves and green pistachios being toasted together in a dry black kadai

steps.title: Chop the nuts
steps.text: Pulse the cooled nuts in the mixer, or chop them with a knife, into small pieces; don't grind them to a powder.
steps.visual: Coarsely chopped mixed nuts in a mixer jar, pistachio green flecks visible

steps.title: Mash the dates
steps.text: Pulse the seeded dates in the mixer to a thick, sticky paste.
steps.visual: A thick, sticky dark-brown date paste in the mixer jar

steps.title: Cook the date paste
steps.text: Heat the ghee in the kadai on low heat, add the date paste and cardamom and stir for 3 to 4 minutes until it softens, turns glossy and comes together as one mass.
steps.visual: A glossy mass of date paste being stirred with ghee in the black kadai

steps.title: Fold in the nuts
steps.text: Add the chopped nuts and mix for 1 minute until evenly distributed, then turn off the heat and let it cool until comfortable to handle.
steps.visual: Chopped nuts folded through the glossy date paste in the kadai, chunks visible throughout

steps.title: Shape and coat
steps.text: With greased palms, roll into 12 ladoos and roll each one in desiccated coconut. Leave for 10 minutes to firm up.
steps.visual: Date and nut ladoos being rolled in white desiccated coconut, finished ones on a steel plate

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve one ladoo as a sweet after a meal.
steps.visual: A coconut-coated date and nut ladoo cut in half on a small plate, showing chunks of almond, cashew and pistachio

substitutions.note: Pumpkin seeds keep the crunch and cost less.
Use coconut oil to make it vegan.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight box for up to 3 weeks.

recipes.title: Apple–Cinnamon Baked Oats
recipes.description: A soft, sliceable bake of oats, grated apple, milk and egg with cinnamon, walnuts and a few raisins for sweetness. Serve warm as a dessert or breakfast; cuts into 4 squares.

steps.title: Preheat and grease
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a small baking dish or tray, about 6 to 7 inches across, with the ghee.
steps.visual: A small square baking tray brushed with a thin film of ghee, an oven glowing behind it

steps.title: Whisk the wet mix
steps.text: In a bowl, whisk the milk, egg and vanilla, if using, until smooth.
steps.visual: Milk and egg whisked together until frothy in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Add oats and spice
