steps.text: Stir in the oats, cinnamon, baking powder and salt.
steps.visual: Rolled oats soaking in the cinnamon-flecked milk mixture in the steel bowl

steps.title: Fold in apple and raisins
steps.text: Fold in the grated apple and the raisins.
steps.visual: Shreds of pale grated apple and dark raisins folded through the oat mixture in the steel bowl

steps.title: Fill the dish
steps.text: Pour into the greased dish, level the top and scatter over the chopped walnuts.
steps.visual: The oat and apple mixture levelled in the greased baking tray, chopped walnuts scattered over the surface

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake at 180°C for 25 to 28 minutes until set in the centre and golden on top.
steps.visual: A golden, set apple-oat bake in its tray inside the oven, walnuts toasted on top

steps.title: Cut and serve
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into 4 squares. Serve warm on its own or with a spoon of curd.
steps.visual: A warm square of apple-cinnamon baked oats on a plate showing apple shreds and raisins inside, a spoon of curd beside it

substitutions.note: Use ½ mashed banana in place of the egg; the bake is softer and sweeter.
Chopped dates work too; both are concentrated fruit sugar, so keep to the same small amount.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Microwave a square for 40 seconds.

recipes.title: Elaichi Shrikhand (Lightly Sweetened)
recipes.description: Thick hung curd whipped with a modest amount of powdered sugar and cardamom and topped with pistachios. The Maharashtrian and Gujarati classic, made with well under half the usual sugar.

ingredients.prep: from about 800 g curd strained overnight, or thick Greek yogurt

steps.title: Hang the curd
steps.text: If making your own, tie about 800 g curd in a muslin cloth and hang it over a bowl in the fridge for 6 to 8 hours until thick and spreadable. Discard or drink the whey.
steps.visual: A muslin bundle of thick white hung curd opened in a steel mixing bowl, a little whey pooled in a separate cup

steps.title: Whip until smooth
steps.text: Whisk the hung curd for 1 to 2 minutes until completely smooth and glossy, with no grainy lumps.
steps.visual: Smooth, glossy, thick white curd being whisked in the steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Sweeten and flavour
steps.text: Add the powdered sugar, cardamom and milk and whisk until the sugar dissolves. Taste; it should be gently sweet and tangy.
steps.visual: Creamy pale shrikhand flecked with ground cardamom in the steel bowl, the whisk lifting a thick ribbon

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and chill for at least 1 hour so the flavours settle and it firms up.
steps.visual: The covered steel bowl of shrikhand on a fridge shelf

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon into small bowls, about 100 g each, and top with slivered pistachios.
steps.visual: Small glass bowls of thick, creamy shrikhand topped with green pistachio slivers

substitutions.note: Honey or powdered jaggery can replace the sugar, but both are sugars too; keep the amount small.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Mango–Chia Pudding
recipes.description: Chia seeds set overnight in cardamom milk, layered with fresh mango purée and diced mango. Sweetened only by ripe fruit, with no added sugar.

steps.title: Whisk chia into milk
steps.text: Whisk the chia seeds into the milk with the cardamom in a bowl.
steps.visual: Black chia seeds suspended in milk being whisked in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Whisk again
steps.text: Leave for 10 minutes, then whisk again to break up any clumps of seeds.
steps.visual: The chia milk starting to thicken in the steel bowl, seeds evenly spread

steps.title: Chill to set
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until thick and spoonable.
steps.visual: The covered bowl of thick, set chia pudding on a fridge shelf

steps.title: Purée the mango
steps.text: Blend half the mango to a smooth purée and dice the rest.
steps.visual: Bright orange mango purée in a blender jar beside a small pile of diced mango on a board

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spoon a layer of mango purée into two glasses, top with the chia pudding and finish with the diced mango.
steps.visual: Two glasses showing a layer of orange mango purée, a speckled layer of chia pudding and diced mango on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Scatter with chopped pistachios if you like and serve chilled.
steps.visual: A glass of layered mango–chia pudding topped with diced mango and green pistachio, a long spoon beside it

substitutions.note: Coconut milk diluted with water makes it dairy-free.

recipes.storage: The set chia keeps 2 days refrigerated; add the mango on the day.

recipes.title: Masala Chaas (Spiced Buttermilk)
recipes.description: Chilled, thin buttermilk blended with roasted cumin, ginger, green chilli, mint and coriander and seasoned with black salt. A cooling drink alongside a spicy lunch.

steps.title: Roast the cumin
steps.text: Dry roast the cumin seeds on a tawa over low heat for about 1 minute until they darken slightly and smell toasty. Crush them coarsely.
steps.visual: Darkened cumin seeds on a small black tawa, a few crushed in a mortar beside it

steps.title: Blend the herbs
steps.text: Blend the ginger, green chilli, mint and coriander with 2 tbsp of the water to a smooth green paste.
steps.visual: A bright green paste of mint, coriander, ginger and chilli at the bottom of a blender jar

steps.title: Blend with curd
steps.text: Add the curd, the rest of the chilled water, black salt, salt and most of the roasted cumin. Blend for 20 seconds until frothy.
steps.visual: Frothy, pale-green buttermilk filling the blender jar, flecked with herbs and cumin

steps.title: Serve chilled
steps.text: Pour into glasses, sprinkle with the remaining cumin and serve cold.
steps.visual: Two tall steel tumblers of frothy masala chaas sprinkled with roasted cumin, a mint sprig on top

substitutions.note: Slightly sour curd gives the best flavour; very fresh curd makes a milder chaas.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 day refrigerated; stir or re-blend before serving.

recipes.title: Haldi Doodh (Turmeric Milk)
recipes.description: Warm milk simmered with turmeric, a pinch of black pepper, ginger, cinnamon and cardamom. A comforting bedtime drink; sweeten lightly with jaggery only if you like.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Crush the ginger, cinnamon and cardamom lightly in a mortar so they release their flavour.
steps.visual: Crushed ginger, a broken cinnamon stick and split cardamom pods in a small stone mortar

steps.title: Warm the milk
steps.text: Pour the milk into a saucepan, add the crushed spices and heat on medium until it starts to steam.
steps.visual: Milk steaming gently in a steel saucepan with ginger, cinnamon and cardamom floating in it

steps.title: Simmer with turmeric
steps.text: Whisk in the turmeric and black pepper and simmer on low heat for 5 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't boil over.
steps.visual: Bright golden-yellow milk simmering in the saucepan, a whisk resting against the rim

steps.title: Sweeten if you like
steps.text: Turn off the heat and stir in the jaggery, if using, until dissolved.
steps.visual: A spoonful of grated jaggery melting into the golden milk in the saucepan off the heat

steps.title: Strain and serve
steps.text: Strain into cups and serve warm.
steps.visual: Two cups of warm golden turmeric milk with a light froth, a cinnamon stick on the saucer

substitutions.note: For a dairy-free version, use coconut milk diluted with water.

recipes.storage: Best made fresh.

recipes.title: Spinach–Banana Curd Smoothie
recipes.description: A bright green smoothie of fresh spinach, ripe banana, curd, flax seeds and mint. Ready in five minutes; the banana masks the spinach, so it tastes mild and fruity.

steps.title: Wash the greens
steps.text: Wash the spinach and mint well in a bowl of water to remove any grit, and drain.
steps.visual: Fresh spinach leaves and mint sprigs drained in a steel colander, still wet

steps.title: Slice the banana
steps.text: Peel and slice the bananas. Frozen banana makes the smoothie thicker and colder.
steps.visual: Sliced banana coins on a wooden board next to the drained greens

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Put the spinach, mint, banana, curd, water, flax seeds and lemon juice in a blender and blend for about 1 minute until completely smooth.
steps.visual: A blender jar full of smooth, vivid green smoothie with a frothy top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Taste and blend in honey only if you need it. Pour into glasses and drink straight away.
steps.visual: Two glasses of thick, bright green spinach–banana smoothie, a banana slice on each rim

substitutions.note: Milk gives a sweeter, thinner smoothie.
Chia seeds thicken it a little more.

recipes.storage: Drink fresh; the colour dulls after an hour.

recipes.title: Banana–Peanut Butter Smoothie
recipes.description: A thick, creamy smoothie of banana, unsweetened peanut butter, milk and hung curd with a little cinnamon. Filling enough for a quick breakfast or an after-exercise snack.

steps.title: Slice the banana
steps.text: Peel and slice the banana into the blender jar.
steps.visual: Banana coins dropped into an empty blender jar

steps.title: Add everything else
steps.text: Add the peanut butter, milk, hung curd and cinnamon, plus the cocoa powder if you want a chocolate version.
steps.visual: Banana slices, a dollop of peanut butter and thick white hung curd under milk in the blender jar, cinnamon dusted on top

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend for 45 seconds to 1 minute until thick and completely smooth. Add a splash of water if it's too thick to pour.
steps.visual: A blender jar of thick, creamy, pale-tan smoothie with a smooth, frothy surface

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into glasses and serve straight away.
steps.visual: Two glasses of thick banana–peanut butter smoothie dusted with cinnamon, a banana half beside them

substitutions.note: Soak 12 almonds overnight and blend them in for a peanut-free version.
Regular curd makes a thinner smoothie with less protein.

recipes.storage: Drink fresh; it thickens and darkens on standing.

recipes.title: Kabuli Chana Chaat Salad Jars
recipes.description: Meal-prep jars of pressure-cooked chickpeas layered with cucumber, tomato, capsicum, carrot and onion over a lemon–chaat masala dressing, topped with pomegranate and seeds. Makes 3 jars that keep for 3 days.

steps.title: Soak the chickpeas
steps.text: Wash the chickpeas and soak them in plenty of water overnight, at least 8 hours. They will roughly double in size.
steps.visual: Plump, beige chickpeas soaking under water in a large steel bowl

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Drain, add the chickpeas to the pressure cooker with the fresh water and half the salt, and cook on medium heat for 4 to 5 whistles, then let the pressure drop naturally. They should be tender but hold their shape. Drain and cool completely.
steps.visual: Tender, whole cooked chickpeas being drained in a steel colander over the open pressure cooker

steps.title: Mix the dressing
steps.text: Whisk the lemon juice with the chaat masala, roasted cumin, chilli powder, green chilli and the remaining salt.
steps.visual: A small steel bowl of reddish-brown lemon and chaat masala dressing with chopped green chilli

steps.title: Chop the vegetables
steps.text: Dice the onion, carrot, capsicum, cucumber and tomato into small, even pieces and chop the herbs.
steps.visual: Neat piles of diced onion, orange carrot, green capsicum, cucumber, red tomato and chopped coriander and mint on a wooden board

steps.title: Layer the jars
steps.text: Divide the dressing between three jars. Layer in the chickpeas, then onion, carrot and capsicum, then cucumber and tomato, and finish with the herbs, pomegranate and sunflower seeds. Keeping the dressing at the bottom stops the vegetables going soggy.
steps.visual: Three glass jars showing neat layers of dressing, chickpeas, orange carrot, green capsicum, cucumber and red tomato, topped with pomegranate and seeds

steps.title: Shake and serve
steps.text: To eat, shake the closed jar or tip it into a bowl and toss well.
steps.visual: A bowl of tossed chickpea chaat salad with colourful vegetables and pomegranate, an emptied jar beside it

substitutions.note: Black chickpeas are cheaper and firmer; cook for 6 to 7 whistles.
Roasted peanuts add crunch for less money.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated in closed jars; keep the tomato away from the dressing so it stays firm.

recipes.title: Chicken, Vegetable & Brown Rice Meal-Prep Bowls
recipes.description: Four lunch boxes of tandoori-spiced chicken breast, pressure-cooked brown rice and quickly sautéed broccoli, beans and carrot. Cook once at the weekend for 3 to 4 days of lunches.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the chicken with the curd, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli, turmeric, garam masala, cumin, lemon juice and half the salt. Cover and leave for 30 minutes, or refrigerate overnight.
steps.visual: Chicken breast pieces coated in a thick orange-red curd marinade in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Cook the brown rice
steps.text: While the chicken marinates, rinse the brown rice and soak it in the measured water in the pressure cooker for 30 minutes. Cook on medium heat for 4 whistles, then 5 minutes on low, and let the pressure drop naturally.
steps.visual: The opened pressure cooker showing fluffy, cooked brown rice with steam rising

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Cut the broccoli into small florets, the beans into 1-inch pieces and the carrot into diagonal slices.
steps.visual: Green broccoli florets, cut beans and orange carrot slices in three heaps on a wooden board

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Heat two-thirds of the oil in a non-stick pan on medium heat. Cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes per side until charred in spots and cooked through, with clear juices and no pink in the centre. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces with charred orange-red edges searing in a non-stick pan

steps.title: Sauté the vegetables
steps.text: Add the remaining oil to the same pan, then the vegetables, the rest of the salt, the pepper and 2 tbsp water. Toss on high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until bright and just tender-crisp.
steps.visual: Bright green broccoli, beans and orange carrot glistening with crushed pepper in the pan

steps.title: Cool and portion
steps.text: Cool everything for 15 to 20 minutes, then divide the rice, sliced chicken and vegetables between 4 lunch boxes and sprinkle with coriander. Close and refrigerate within an hour of cooking.
steps.visual: Four open lunch boxes, each with brown rice, sliced tandoori chicken and a section of broccoli, beans and carrot, topped with coriander

steps.title: Reheat and serve
steps.text: Reheat a box until steaming hot all the way through and eat with a spoon of curd or green chutney.
steps.visual: A reheated meal-prep bowl of brown rice, sliced spiced chicken and vegetables with a spoonful of green chutney

substitutions.note: Boneless thigh stays juicier on reheating; it has a little more fat.
Foxtail millet cooks in 2 whistles and has a similar amount of fibre.
For a vegetarian box, marinate paneer the same way and sear it for 2 minutes per side.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Cool and refrigerate within an hour of cooking.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle the rice with 1 tbsp water and microwave covered for 2 to 2½ minutes until steaming hot throughout.

recipes.title: Paneer & Vegetable Foxtail Millet Bowls
recipes.description: Fluffy foxtail millet topped with cumin–pepper paneer, sautéed capsicum, red pepper, onion and spinach, finished with lemon and toasted sesame. Packs into 3 lunch boxes.

steps.title: Rinse and soak the millet
steps.text: Rinse the foxtail millet 3 to 4 times and soak it in fresh water for 30 minutes, then drain.
steps.visual: Pale-yellow foxtail millet soaking under clear water in a steel bowl

steps.title: Cook the millet
steps.text: Bring the measured water and half the salt to a boil in a saucepan, add the millet, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Rest 5 minutes and fluff. In a pressure cooker, cook for 2 whistles.
steps.visual: Fluffy, cooked foxtail millet being lifted with a fork in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Slice the onion and garlic, dice the capsicum and red pepper, and roughly chop the spinach.
steps.visual: Sliced onion and garlic, green capsicum and red pepper dice and a heap of chopped spinach on a wooden board

steps.title: Sear the paneer
steps.text: Heat the oil in a non-stick pan on medium heat, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle. Add the paneer, sprinkle with turmeric, Kashmiri chilli, pepper and a pinch of salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Lift out onto a plate.
steps.visual: Golden, spice-flecked paneer cubes with cumin seeds in a non-stick pan

steps.title: Sauté the vegetables
steps.text: In the same pan, sauté the onion and garlic for 2 minutes, add the capsicum and red pepper with the remaining salt and toss on high heat for 2 minutes. Add the spinach and stir for 1 minute until just wilted. Return the paneer to the pan.
steps.visual: Green and red peppers, soft onion and wilted spinach tossed with the golden paneer cubes in the pan

steps.title: Assemble the bowls
steps.text: Divide the millet between 3 bowls or lunch boxes, spoon over the paneer and vegetables, and finish with the lemon juice, toasted sesame and coriander.
steps.visual: Three lunch boxes of pale-gold millet topped with paneer cubes, red and green peppers and spinach, sprinkled with sesame and coriander

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Eat warm, or refrigerate and reheat for lunch. A spoon of curd or green chutney goes well alongside.
steps.visual: A paneer and vegetable millet bowl with a small pot of green chutney beside it and a spoon resting in the bowl

substitutions.note: Firm tofu, pressed dry, makes it vegan.
Little millet works the same way with slightly less water.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and microwave covered for 2 minutes until hot throughout.
